content.text: {"headline":"Approve R1: earlier overtime plus wider chat deflection. It gives the best recovery available (75.7% vs 80% target) for ₹9,762, but it still falls short of target.","why":"Payments calls jumped to +52% above forecast after the 10:55 reward-points email, and service level fell to 32%. Doing nothing leaves the 11:45-15:15 window at 40.4% (Payments 29.3%) with 15.7% abandons. No plan reaches 80% over the window. R1 comes closest at 75.7% (Payments 73.3%, General 79.8%) and cuts abandons to 6.2%. It does this by starting overtime at 11:45 (35 agents to 13:45, then 22 to 15:15) and deflecting 20% of refund-status, payment-status and new-offer enquiries to chat. Rest-of-day service level reaches 85.4%.","trade_offs":["Cost: ₹9,762, the most expensive option along with R2. That is ₹300 more than P4 (67.4%) and ₹2,400 more than P3 (63.0%), for 8-13 points more service level.","R2 costs the same but does worse (73.0% overall, General 76.2%) because it pulls 5 agents from General at 15:00 rather than 3.","Risk to General: R1 still moves 3 cross-skilled agents to Payments from 15:00 to 16:00, but General is predicted at 79.8%, better than with no action (61.5%).","Customer impact: R1 drops IVR callback and break delays. Chat deflection steers some callers to chat. Payments coaching from 15:30 to 16:00 is cancelled.","The no-cost options (P1 37.4%, P2 42.0%) barely move service level, and P1 is worse than doing nothing."],"watch":"R1 depends on enough agents accepting the overtime from 11:45. If take-up is low, service level will stay well below 75.7%. Confirm the reward-email calls really are Payments demand (the diagnosis confidence is medium), and check whether the surge eases after 12:00. Keep an eye on General after 15:00 when the 3 agents move across."}
